title: Grammar — Κεφάλαιον Βʹ (The Garden and the Animals)

sections.heading: 1. Neuter 2nd-Declension Nouns
sections.content: Neuter nouns of the 2nd declension differ from masculine ones chiefly in the nominative and accusative, which are identical (ending -ον singular, -α plural). The article is τό (singular) and τά (plural).

examples.greek: ἐν τῷ κήπῳ ἐστὶν τὰ δένδρα
examples.note: the trees are in the garden

sections.heading: 2. The Neuter Plural Rule
sections.content: A distinctive rule of Greek: neuter plural subjects regularly take a singular verb. This applies to all neuter nouns regardless of declension.

examples.greek: τὰ πρόβατα ἐστιν ἐν τῷ κήπῳ
examples.note: the sheep are in the garden

sections.heading: 3. Masculine Plural — Nominative and Accusative
sections.content: Masculine 2nd-declension nouns in the plural use -οι (nominative) and -ους (accusative). The article is οἱ (nominative) and τούς (accusative).

sections.heading: 4. Present Active Indicative — 3rd Person Plural
sections.content: The 3rd plural ending is -ουσι(ν): they do. Contract verbs in -έω contract the stem vowel: ε + ουσι → -οῦσι.

sections.heading: 5. Complementary Infinitive — θέλω and μέλλω
sections.content: Two verbs introduced in this chapter take a complementary infinitive (an infinitive that completes their meaning). The infinitive of -ω verbs ends in -ειν.

examples.note: he wants to seize the lamb
the wolf is about to flee

sections.heading: 6. The Pronoun αὐτός
sections.content: αὐτός is the 3rd-person personal pronoun. It declines like a 2nd-declension adjective and agrees with its antecedent in gender and number.

examples.greek: ὁ λύκος ἔρχεται. αὐτὸς θέλει ἁρπάζειν τὸ ἀρνίον
examples.note: The wolf comes. He wants to seize the lamb.

sections.heading: 7. Feminine 1st Declension
sections.content: Feminine nouns of the 1st declension end in -η or -α. The article is ἡ (nominative singular), τήν (accusative singular), τῆς (genitive), τῇ (dative).

table.caption: 1st Declension Feminine — ἡ φωνή ("voice") and ἡ ἡμέρα ("day")

examples.note: he hears the voice of the master

sections.heading: 8. New Prepositions: εἰς, ἀπό, ἐπί, ὑπό
sections.content: This chapter introduces several new prepositions, each governing a specific case.

examples.note: under the tree there is shade
